Live monitor

    Leave groups clear to include all available vehicles. Picking a zone type keeps only the events inside that type's zones, and picking zones narrows it to those; leave both clear for everywhere. Selected zones are outlined on the map and named on each event and in the report.
    Instructions
    1. Choose to visualize by location history, exception history or weight history.
    2. In weight history, the cargo weight recorded by each vehicle is mapped over the selected date range and compared with the axle scale register: over the GML payload is an overload, over the GVM payload is critical, and vehicles missing from the register use the Fallback payload limit. Each vehicle's five worst overloads carry a ranked badge.
    3. Tick Live monitor to watch current vehicle positions on the same map, refreshed on the chosen interval. Alerts flash and are listed for vehicles over the speed threshold, over their payload limit, or with a new exception for the selected rules. MyGeotab has no push channel, so freshness is limited by the refresh interval and polling pauses while this tab is hidden.
    4. If visualizing by exception history, select one or more rules to search: speeding rules in the Speeding section, idling rules in the Idling section, and everything else in Other rule(s).
    5. Optionally select a group type and vehicle group, then select the vehicle(s) to search.
    6. Optionally select zone types to narrow the zone list, then select zones to include only records inside them.
    7. In exception history, untick Show heatmap layer to keep exception data and event details without heat colouring.
    8. Tick Show speed limit zones and pick the posted limits (10–110) to overlay the NZTA speed limit zones for the current map view; events inside a zone show that zone's limit on their sign and are counted in the zone legend.
    9. Untick a Speed band to hide the events in it. The bands are your database's Risk Management speed bands (Administration → System Settings), and each event is banded by its peak vehicle speed.
    10. Tick Only the top 5 speeding events per vehicle to ring-fence each vehicle's five fastest speeding events. Those events always carry a ranked badge (#1 is that vehicle's fastest) and a highlighted ring, whether or not the filter is on.
    11. In Idling, choose a minimum event duration and set Fuel L/h and $ / L; every idling event is costed as idle hours × L/h × $/L, and the five costliest per vehicle carry a ranked badge and a highlighted ring. Tick Only the top 5 costliest idling events per vehicle to keep just those.
    12. Tick School zones only to keep just the school zones, and Only events inside the selected zones to search speeding and every other exception within those zones alone.
    13. Specify a date/time range and click Show Results.
    14. Use Refresh data after changing the MyGeotab Groups Filter or when fleet data changes.
    15. Open a Rule or Vehicle dropdown and tick every item you want to include.
